title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Implementation of the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on the Implementation of the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China

Fa Fa [2001] No. 11

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Amending the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China was adopted at the 22nd session of the Standing Committee of the Ninth National People's Congress on June 30, 2001, and shall come into force on January 1, 2002. In order to ensure the implementation of the new Judges Law, the following notice on relevant issues is hereby given:

First, Diligently Carry Out Study and Publicity of the New Judges Law

The amended Judges Law of the People's Republic of China summarizes the experience gained in the construction of the People's Courts since 1995, and has further amended and improved the qualifications for judges, the procedures for appointment and removal, the avoidance system for judges in office, the supervision over the appointment of judges, and the determination of the proportion of judge posts. It is of great significance for establishing a judge system with Chinese characteristics, ensuring that judges perform their duties lawfully, improving the overall quality of the judge contingent, and realizing scientific management of judges. Leaders of People's Courts at all levels must attach great importance to the study and publicity of the new Judges Law. In light of the actual conditions of the People's Courts, specific plans and measures for studying the new Judges Law shall be formulated, so as to study and grasp the legislative intent well and lay a solid foundation for the implementation of the new Judges Law.

Second, Strictly Control the Qualifications for Judges

After the new Judges Law comes into effect, when appointing judges, People's Courts at all levels must strictly comply with the educational qualifications and legal work years requirements stipulated in the new Judges Law. With regard to the provision that "for localities with genuine difficulties, the educational qualification requirement may be relaxed for a certain period," the Supreme People's Court will put forward formal opinions on the basis of investigation and study. Before the Supreme People's Court puts forward such formal opinions, People's Courts at all levels may not on their own relax the conditions to appoint judges. High People's Courts may put forward opinions in light of the actual conditions of their respective regions for the reference of the Supreme People's Court.

Higher-level People's Courts shall, in accordance with the authority over cadres, proactively conduct assessment work for candidates for presidents and vice-presidents of lower-level People's Courts. Where candidates do not meet the qualifications for judges, opinions shall be proactively submitted to local Party committees, and the duty of co-management shall be earnestly fulfilled.

Before the new Judges Law formally takes effect on January 1, 2002, People's Courts at all levels may still appoint or submit for appointment judges in accordance with the qualifications and procedures for judges stipulated in the current Judges Law. When appointing or submitting for appointment of judges, the conditions may not be lowered or the procedures violated.

Third, Strictly Implement the National Judicial Examination System

From January 1, 2002, when People's Courts at all levels supplement candidates for judges, selection must be made on a merit basis from among persons who have passed the National Judicial Examination, and interviews and assessments shall be conducted. When appointing judges, People's Courts at all levels may conduct professional examinations and select the best candidates. When supplementing staff other than judges, People's Courts at all levels must select on a merit basis from among persons who have passed the unified provincial-level examination organized by the national political and legal departments. In addition, persons appointed for the first time as judges or assistant judges, or directly appointed as deputy division chiefs, division chiefs, or members of the judicial committee in People's Courts at all levels, must pass the National Judicial Examination.

Given that the new Judges Law has already provided for the establishment of the National Judicial Examination system, the Judges Appraisal Committee of the Supreme People's Court will not organize a national unified examination for first-appointed judges and assistant judges this year.

Fourth, Strengthen the Inspection and Supervision of Judicial Appointments

People's Courts at all levels must strictly select and appoint judges in accordance with the conditions and procedures stipulated in the new Judges Law. The Supreme People's Court will, in strict compliance with the provisions of the new Judges Law, inspect and supervise the lawful selection and appointment of judges by local People's Courts. Higher-level People's Courts shall conduct regular inspections of the selection and appointment of judges by lower-level People's Courts, and upon discovering problems, shall proactively make recommendations and urge corrections.

The Supreme People's Court has decided that in the second half of this year, a comprehensive inspection shall be carried out nationwide regarding the illegal selection or illegal submission for appointment of judges since July 1, 1995. With respect to persons who were appointed as judges or assistant judges without passing the national unified examination for first-appointed judges and assistant judges, or without possessing a junior college education level, People's Courts at all levels must resolutely remove them or submit to the People's Congress for their removal from judicial posts. High People's Courts must earnestly take responsibility, designate special personnel, strictly enforce laws and discipline, show no leniency or accommodation toward illegal acts, and ensure that this work is not perfunctory. People's Courts at all levels shall combine this inspection with the "one education and three rectifications" campaign, treating it as specific content for rectifying discipline and work style, and ensuring it is implemented and achieved practically. The Supreme People's Court will dispatch inspection teams to conduct spot checks on the implementation of the inspection work. High People's Courts that fail to complete the work as required shall be subject to circulating criticism, and court leaders who, in violation of the provisions of the Judges Law, still illegally submit for appointment of judges or appoint assistant judges shall be dealt with seriously in accordance with Party and administrative discipline. This work shall be completed by the end of December 2001. High People's Courts shall be responsible for submitting written reports to the Supreme People's Court.

Fifth, Carry Out Training Work for the Judge Contingent

The Supreme People's Court will, in accordance with the requirements of the new Judges Law, conduct training for persons in the judge contingent who have not attained the undergraduate education level. Specific training plans will be separately prescribed. High People's Courts shall ascertain the current situation of the judge contingent in their respective regions, study and formulate plans for the next step of training work, and make preparations in terms of training faculty, venues, teaching materials, and other aspects.

Studying, publicizing, and implementing the new Judges Law is an important task related to the construction of the socialist legal system. People's Courts at all levels shall actively report their work to local Party committees and People's Congresses, and seek their support. At the same time, in the course of implementing the new Judges Law, People's Courts at all levels shall continuously summarize experience, earnestly study new problems encountered, put forward opinions, and promptly report to and seek instructions from the Supreme People's Court, so as to ensure the correct implementation of the new Judges Law.

July 11, 2001
